findings.title: Lithuanian account string replaced with Italian text
findings.body: totpStep1 was changed to the Italian sentence 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'. Lithuanian users will see this in the account console's authenticator setup. The PR only needed to drop the FreeOTP/Google Play anchors that the verifier rejects, so the value should be Lithuanian text without the anchors. The verifier cannot catch a wrong-language string because it only checks markup.

findings.title: Lithuanian login string replaced with Italian text
findings.body: loginTotpStep1 was changed to the Italian sentence 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'. Lithuanian users will see Italian on the OTP setup page. The change only needed to remove the anchors the verifier rejects, so the value should be Lithuanian text. The verifier cannot detect this kind of error since it only checks markup.

findings.title: Simplified Chinese account string now contains Traditional Chinese
findings.body: totpStep1 in the zh_CN file was replaced with '在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：', which uses Traditional characters (手機, 安裝, 應用程式, 之一) copied from the zh_TW bundle. Simplified Chinese users will see the wrong script. It should be Simplified Chinese, e.g. 在您的手机上安装以下应用程序之一：

findings.title: error-invalid-multivalued-size uses placeholders the UI bundle will not interpolate
findings.body: The English source was changed from double-brace placeholders to single braces plus an ICU choice: 'Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.' Every other error-* key in this file uses i18next-style {{n}} placeholders (see lines 14, 27, 29), so this bundle appears to be consumed through i18next. In that case {0} and {1} are not substituted and the choice expression is shown literally. The same change in js/apps/admin-ui/maven-resources/theme/keycloak.v2/admin/messages/messages_en.properties (line 3139) has the same problem. Keep the {{n}} form in these React-consumed bundles, or confirm the consumer really uses MessageFormat.

findings.title: Missing English sibling aborts verification with an unchecked exception
findings.body: If the English sibling file cannot be opened, verifySafeHtml throws a RuntimeException. verify() only catches IOException, so the exception escapes and aborts the whole plugin run with a stack trace, rather than reporting a message for the offending file. The rename of duplicate_keys.properties to duplicateKeys_en.properties in this PR is a symptom: the regex maps duplicate_keys.properties to duplicate_en.properties, which does not exist. Missing English counterparts should be reported as messages, not thrown.

findings.body:
The check compares the sanitizer output byte-for-byte with the input. OWASP serializes void elements as '
', so semantically valid markup like '

' is flagged as 'Illegal HTML'. This is why the PR rewrites '
' to '
' in about 40 translation files with no content change. Any translator who writes '
' will get a false failure. Compare normalized output (for example after parsing both sides) or normalize void-element syntax before comparing.

findings.title: Anchor pattern also matches unrelated tags starting with 'a'
findings.body: The pattern '</?a[^>]*>' matches any tag whose name starts with 'a', such as <abbr>, <address>, <article> or <audio>. santizeAnchors then treats these as anchors, which produces misleading 'Didn't find anchor tag' messages and can pair an unrelated tag with a real anchor in the English source. The pattern should require the tag name to end at a word boundary, for example '</?a(\s[^>]*)?>'.

findings.title: Anchor error message omits the key and file
findings.body: The message 'Didn't find anchor tag ... in original string' does not include the message key or the file name. Every other message in this class ('Illegal HTML in key ... for file ...', 'Duplicate keys in file ...') does. A maintainer reading CI output across hundreds of translation files cannot tell which key to fix. Include the key and file path in the message.

findings.title: Tests cover only failure cases and the duplicate-key assertion was weakened
findings.body:
The duplicate-key assertion changed from an exact match to hasItem, and none of the new tests check the passing path. There is no fixture that should produce zero messages: allowed
